project.objective: Besides their children John, Hannah Grace, Edwin, William, and James, did Hannah Earnest and Edwin Grice have any other children? Identify each additional child and their birth details.

questions.question: When was Hannah Earnest born, and does the 30 January 1868 Christening record at Wolverhampton belong to her or to another individual?
questions.rationale: Person-warnings returns two contradiction-severity alerts on Hannah Earnest: her tree records a birth of 1857 yet also carries a Christening dated 30 Jan 1868, while a Residence in 1861 pre-dates that Christening by more than three years — an impossible sequence if all three events belong to the same person. The 1857 birth and the 1868 Christening/Baptism cannot both apply to Hannah Earnest without contradiction. Resolving her true birth year is prerequisite to any completeness question about her children, because the span of her reproductive years determines which censuses and vital-record windows to search. English civil registration (GRO births from 1837), parish registers held by Staffordshire Archives, and the 1861 and 1871 England census records that already place her in the household provide the primary source base for testing this contradiction.

items.rationale: The tree records Hannah's birth year as 1857 in Darlaston but no GRO registration entry has been found or cited. The England and Wales, Birth Registration Index, 1837-2008 (name-searchable) covers this district and period and is the first source to check. Civil registration began 1 July 1837; compliance improved after 1874, so a birth c.1857 should exist but may be filed under a phonetic variant (Arnest, Ernest). The GRO birth index also includes the mother's maiden name from 1837 onwards, which will confirm parentage. Search phonetic variants of Earnest (Ernest, Arnest) and expand to adjacent districts (Walsall, Penkridge) if not found in Wolverhampton. The result will show the registered birth year, the exact quarter, and the district — supplying the anchor date that all other items depend on.

Fallback for the FamilySearch birth index search. Ancestry hosts the England and Wales, Civil Registration Birth Index, 1837-1915 (name-searchable), drawn from the same GRO source. If the FamilySearch index returns nothing under Earnest/Ernest/Arnest across the Wolverhampton and adjacent districts, Ancestry's version should be tried with the same phonetic variants, as the two indexes have been transcribed independently and may carry different errors. The GRO's own free online birth index at gro.gov.uk (includes mother's maiden name) is a further check if both index searches fail.

The tree already records Hannah's 1861 Residence at Darlaston and cites source 9F5F-VZ7 (England and Wales, Census, 1861, entry for Joseph Earnest and Diana Earnest). That source has been attached but not yet extracted: the census image must be read to record the age stated for Hannah in April 1861, which is the earliest documentary age evidence predating the 1868 christening. If the 1861 return gives her age as approximately 3-4 she was born c.1857-58, consistent with the tree; if it gives 1-2 she was born c.1859-60, which would put the 1868 christening only eight or nine years after birth — still plausible for Victorian delayed baptism, but narrowing the window. The England and Wales, Census, 1861 collection is name-searchable. The 1861 census is the dependency that sets the outer birth-year boundary for the GRO search.

The tree records Hannah's 1871 Residence at Wolverhampton and cites source 9V1G-YQQ (England and Wales, Census, 1871, entry for Joseph Hirnist and Dianah Hirnist — note the heavy phonetic distortion of the surname Earnest/Ernest to Hirnist). That source is attached but not yet extracted. Reading the 1871 household image gives Hannah's stated age in April 1871, providing a second independent age witness. Combined with the 1861 age, the two censuses bracket her birth year. The 1871 entry also locates the family in Wolverhampton, confirming the geographic context for the January 1868 christening at St John Wolverhampton. The England and Wales, Census, 1871 collection is name-searchable. Note the variant spelling; search as Hirnist and Ernest.

The tree carries two overlapping fact entries for the 30 January 1868 event: a Baptism at Wolverhampton and a Christening at St John, Wolverhampton, both citing source SWZ4-P1R (England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538-1944). That source has been attached but not yet extracted. The image of the actual register entry must be read to answer the core question: does the entry state a birth date or age for the child, and is the child's father named as Joseph Ernest/Earnest? The Staffordshire Church Records collection (id 2364451) is name-searchable. Victorian Anglican baptism registers in this period used the standard register format that recorded the child's birth date in a separate column from the baptism date — reading that column resolves whether the stated birth date is consistent with 1857 or contradicts it. The loc_001 quirk notes that St Peter's (the ancient mother church) subdivided into daughter parishes by 1849; St John is one of those daughters, so the search must be scoped to that specific parish.

Fallback for item 5. FindMyPast hosts Staffordshire Baptisms, 1538-1900 (name-searchable), a separate transcription of the same Staffordshire parish register series. If the FamilySearch Staffordshire Church Records index does not surface the 30 January 1868 entry or does not link to the register image, the FindMyPast version may carry a different transcription or link to the image via a different route. Also consider FreeReg (freereg.org.uk) as a no-cost alternative transcription for the same parish. The loc_001 quirk notes that Nonconformist baptism registers are not in the CoE FamilySearch collection; if the family is identified as Nonconformist (Diana Haines was baptised Wesleyan at Wednesbury in 1828), check the England and Wales, Non-Conformist Record Indexes (RG4-8), 1588-1977 on FamilySearch, though this collection covers pre-1837 registered congregations and may not hold post-1837 Wesleyan records.

The tree records a 1881 Residence for Hannah at West Bromwich (not Wolverhampton) and cites source QYLW-S5N (England and Wales, Census, 1881, entry for Edwin Grice and Hannah Grice). That source is attached but not yet extracted. Reading the 1881 census image gives Hannah's stated age as wife of Edwin Grice, providing a third independent age witness — triangulating between the 1861 and 1871 census ages. It also establishes the number and ages of children present in 1881, which is directly relevant to the project's main objective of identifying additional Grice children (a child absent from the 1881 household but present in 1871 or 1891 would be a candidate for an unrecorded death or a mis-attributed record). The England and Wales, Census, 1881 collection is name-searchable.

The tree records a 1891 Residence for Hannah at Birmingham and cites source 7BL6-KLH (England and Wales, Census, 1891, entry for Edwin Grice and Hannah Grice). That source is attached but not yet extracted. Reading the 1891 census image gives Hannah's stated age as a fourth and later-life age witness, and — crucially for the project objective — establishes the full list of children living in the household in 1891. Any Grice child appearing in 1881 but absent in 1891 (with no death record traced) or any child appearing in 1891 not in the current tree is an answer to the completeness question. The loc_001 quirk notes the BMSGH 1891 Wolverhampton district index on film 6393534 covers Bilston, Tettenhall, Wednesfield, Willenhall and Wombourn — but the family had moved to Birmingham by 1891 so the Warwickshire census applies. The England and Wales, Census, 1891 collection is name-searchable.

FAN item required for an identity and completeness question. The known Grice children span 1877-1886 (John, Hannah Grace, Edwin, William, James). The England and Wales, Birth Registration Index, 1837-2008 (name-searchable) should be searched for all births registered to Grice in the Wolverhampton, Walsall, and West Bromwich districts between 1876 and approximately 1895, to test whether additional children were registered but are absent from the tree. A re-used given name within the family (per the loc_001 quirk) signals an earlier child of that name died; comparing the GRO index against the five known children may surface unregistered siblings. The date window is sized to span the parents' plausible fertility period: Hannah born c.1857 and Edwin born c.1854, so children from c.1876 to c.1895 are realistic. This item is a prerequisite to the project objective and feeds directly into the main completeness question.

Companion FAN item: search the England and Wales, Death Registration Index 1837-2007 (name-searchable) for deaths of children surnamed Grice in the West Bromwich, Wolverhampton, and Birmingham districts between 1876 and 1895. The loc_001 quirk on re-used given names means a second child named 'Hannah' in the family would indicate the first Hannah Grace died; a death-index search for infant Grices in this period will either confirm known deaths or surface unrecorded ones. A child born and registered in item 9's search but not traceable in any later census would have a death entry here. This item is bounded by the parents' residential history (West Bromwich from c.1877, Birmingham from c.1891) and the oldest known child's birth year (1877).

log.notes: No match for Hannah Earnest birth registration; all 6 results scored below 0.01 and are from unrelated people/places. Will retry with 'Ernest' spelling.
Found Hannah Earnest in household of Joseph Earnest, 1861 census, Darlaston. Birth year indexed as 1858. Score 0.72, already attached to subject 9DJ7-219.
Retry with Ernest spelling + Staffordshire birthPlace still yielded no match (all below 0.01). Same unrelated 6 results. Will try GRO birth registration index without place restriction.
Zero results for Hannah Ernest in Wolverhampton 1871. Family known to be indexed as 'Hirnist' — will retry with that spelling.

Found Hannah Hirnist (b.1857 Darlaston) as rank 1 (score 0.38), already attached to subject. 1871 census, Household of Joseph Hirnist, Wolverhampton. Record ark:/61903/1:1:V5RF-F7V. Search used 'Hirnist' spelling per known indexing distortion.

Found 30 Jan 1868 baptism of Hannah Ernest, Wolverhampton (rank 1, score 0.756, attached to subject): ark:/61903/1:1:QL3T-C612. Also found marriage record Hannah Ernest & Edwin Grice at West Bromwich (birth year 1856 on that record): ark:/61903/1:1:QLQH-5V5Z.

Found Hannah Grice (b.1857 Darlaston), wife in Household of Edwin Grice, West Bromwich 1881 (rank 1, score 0.394, attached to subject): ark:/61903/1:1:Q27F-Z34M. Record ark QLS8-M521 — same household as Hannah Grice b.1880 (daughter Hannah Grace).

Found Hannah Grice (b.1855 Staffordshire), wife in Household of Edwin Grice, Birmingham 1891 (rank 1, score 0.076, attached to subject): ark:/61903/1:1:WLSD-QPZ. Different birth year from other records (1855 vs 1857/1858) — expected census age rounding variation.

Key finds with father Edwin Grice in Staffordshire: Lydia Grice (bapt 8 Aug 1878, West Bromwich, ark:QL3R-C5SR) — NOT in tree; Hannah Grice (b.3 Apr 1880, bapt 5 May 1880, West Bromwich, = Hannah Grace); William Grice (b.12 Jul 1884, bapt 30 Jul 1884, West Bromwich); James Grice (b.10 Oct 1886, bapt 27 Oct 1886, West Bromwich); Fanny Grice (b.15 Feb 1889, bapt 6 Mar 1889, West Bromwich, ark:QL3R-6ZDW) — NOT in tree. Henry Grice (christened 6 Dec 1879, Harborne, ark:NX6G-69C) needs verification. Total matches 3249 — results not exhausted.

6453 total Grice deaths in Staffordshire 1876-1900 — too broad. None of first 20 match expected children of Edwin/Hannah Grice. Need targeted follow-up searches for Lydia Grice and Fanny Grice specifically.
Targeted search for Lydia Grice death 1878-1895, England: no Lydia Grice match in first 20 results. Lydia appears in 1891 census at age 12, so she survived into adolescence.

Found Fanny Grice, born 1889, died 1890, Birmingham, Warwickshire (ark:2JF2-BCK). Matches Fanny Grice born 15 Feb 1889, who does not appear in 1891 census. This is the death of the Fanny Grice christened 6 Mar 1889 in West Bromwich, daughter of Edwin Grice.

Search for John Grice birth 1875-1879, father Edwin Grice: no confident Staffordshire match in first 20 results. John appears in 1881 and 1891 censuses as b.1877 in West Bromwich. Will search Staffordshire Church Records specifically.

Searched England and Wales Death Registration Index for Hannah Grice to find Hannah Grace Grice (b.~1880) who appears in 1881 census but not 1891. Top result is Hannah Grice b.1856 d.1888 West Bromwich — likely the mother, not the daughter. No clear match for daughter Hannah Grace.

Searched 1901 England & Wales Census for Edwin Grice (father, b.~1854). No confident match for the father. Rank 4 is Edwin Grice b.1883 Darlaston in John Grice's household — the son Edwin (PQQT-5G1), not the father. Father Edwin may have died pre-1901 or be in a different location.

Searched 1911 England & Wales Census for Edwin Grice. Second-best match is son Edwin Grice b.1883 Darlaston with own household. No match for the father. Need to search on Hannah Grice (wife) to find the 1911 household and get children-born/children-living counts.
Searched Staffordshire Church Records for John Grice baptism, father Edwin Grice, b.~1877. 65 results; top 20 examined. No definitive match for John's own baptism found. Will expand search.

Searched 1901 England & Wales Census for Hannah Grice (wife of Edwin, our subject 9DJ7-219). 185 results; no candidate scored above 0.01 against the subject. Top match is Hannah Grice b.1852 Quarry Bank in Edwin Grice household — wrong birth year and birth place. Hannah Earnest (b.~1857, Darlaston) is not confidently identified in this result set. May need broader search or search under widowed status.

Searched 1911 England & Wales Census for Hannah Grice (wife of Edwin, our subject 9DJ7-219). No candidate scored above 0.01. Rank 2 is interesting: Hannah Grice b.1887 West Bromwich in 'Household of James Grice', West Bromwich All Saints — this could be a previously unknown daughter of Edwin and Hannah Earnest (born between James 1886 and Fanny 1889). Will read this record.

Searched Staffordshire Church Records for Grice children baptized 1889-1897 with father Edwin, in West Bromwich. Only definitive match is Fanny Grice (already extracted as src_011). No additional baptisms of Grice children with father Edwin in West Bromwich found in this date range. Remaining results are burials from other Staffordshire parishes or unrelated Edwin Grice families.

Read Henry Grice christening record (NX6G-69C), Harborne, 6 Dec 1879. Father is Edwin Grice; mother is Elizabeth (not Hannah). This is a different Edwin Grice family. Henry Grice is ruled out as a child of Edwin Grice and Hannah Earnest.

Read XWWD-FMH, the 'Household of James Grice' (1911, West Bromwich All Saints). Head is James Grice b.1855, West Bromwich, WIDOWED. His children are Hannah (b.1887), Sid (b.1891), Kate (b.1892), Eva (b.1895), Harold (b.1897). This is a completely different James Grice family — the head is born 1855, the same generation as our Edwin Grice. This family is NOT the household of our son James Grice. Hannah b.1887 West Bromwich here is a daughter of this other James Grice, not of Edwin Grice and Hannah Earnest.

Searched 1901 census for Hannah Grice, widowed, b.1854-1862. Only 3 results, none matching Hannah Earnest (b.~1857, Darlaston). All three are males or clearly wrong people. If Hannah was widowed in 1901 she is not indexed under these criteria.

Searched death index for Edwin Grice, b.1850-1858, death 1891-1905. Only 3 results: top is Edwin Grice died 1899 in Tamworth, Staffordshire (ark:/61903/1:1:2J5W-MR2). Tamworth is in Staffordshire but not West Bromwich. Will read this record to determine if it could be our Edwin Grice.

Searched 1901 census for William Grice, b.1882-1888. Two strong candidates: William Grice b.1885 West Bromwich (XSZ7-6PF) and William Grice b.1886 West Bromwich (XSZF-MJZ), both in 'Household of John Grice', Birmingham. These are almost certainly our William Grice (PQQT-GJC) living with brother John. Confirms parents were not in John's household. Will read this record.

Read possible Edwin Grice death record (2J5W-MR2): Edwin Grice died 1899, Tamworth, Staffordshire. No age or birth details in the index entry. Tamworth is ~20 miles from West Bromwich. Possible match for Edwin Grice (father, b.~1854) but cannot confirm without reading the original death certificate. If confirmed, it would explain why Edwin is absent from all post-1891 censuses.

Read the 1901 John Grice household (XSZ7-6PF). Confirms John Grice (b.1877, West Bromwich, head), wife Bertha (b.1879, Birmingham), and living with them: Edwin Grice (b.1883, Darlaston), William Grice (b.1885, West Bromwich), James Grice (b.1887, West Bromwich). These three brothers all single, working as labourers. Parents Edwin and Hannah are NOT in this household. John also has own children (Gertrude b.1898, John b.1899, Albert b.1901).

Searched death index for Hannah Grice b.1878-1882, died 1881-1892. Two key candidates: (1) Hannah Grice b.1880 d.1881 Walsall (2JD2-9FY) — likely Hannah Grace (b.3 Apr 1880, tree 9DJ7-2B2) who died after the April 1881 census; (2) Hannah Grice b.1882 d.1883 West Bromwich (2JD1-Q7B) — potentially a previously unknown second child named Hannah, born 1882 and dying 1883 before Edwin (b.1883). Will read both records.

Read death record 2JD2-9FY: Hannah Grice, b.1880, d.1881, Walsall, Staffordshire. Most likely Hannah Grace Grice (tree 9DJ7-2B2, b.3 Apr 1880). She appeared in the April 1881 census and died later in 1881 in the Walsall registration district (adjacent to West Bromwich). Will extract.

Read death record 2JD1-Q7B: Hannah Grice, b.1882, d.1883, West Bromwich, Staffordshire. Previously unknown second daughter named Hannah born 1882 after the first Hannah Grace died in 1881 — Victorian re-use of a deceased child's given name. Will extract.

Searched England and Wales Birth Registration Index (2285338) for Grice births in West Bromwich, father Edwin, 1878-1889. Zero results. The collection may not index father names for this period/area. Staffordshire Church Records are the primary evidence source for births in this family.

Searched Staffordshire Church Records for Grice baptisms, father Edwin, West Bromwich, 1879-1888. Top results confirm already-known children: William (b.12 Jul 1884, QL3R-X2D1), James (b.10 Oct 1886, QL3R-V43N), Hannah Grace (b.3 Apr 1880, QL3R-VWY9). Also found: Emma Grice (b.4 Feb 1879, West Bromwich, QL3R-KYXS) and Thomas Grice (b.7 Oct 1879, West Bromwich, QL3R-VJNJ) with father listed as 'Grice' only (given name not indexed) — need to read records to determine if father is our Edwin.

Searched death index for all Grice deaths in West Bromwich 1876-1891. 185 results; top 20 examined. Key candidate: Martha Emily Grice (b.1885, d.1887, West Bromwich, 2JGX-TXK) — if from our family, born between William (Jul 1884) and James (Oct 1886), died before 1891 census. Also Hannah Grice b.1856 d.1888 West Bromwich is likely the mother (not a child), consistent with 1888 death. Will read Martha Emily and Emma Grice records to check parents.
Read Emma Grice baptism (QL3R-KYXS), West Bromwich, 4 Feb 1879. Mother is Harriet, NOT Hannah. This is a different Grice family. Emma is not a child of Edwin Grice and Hannah Earnest. Ruled out.
Read Thomas Grice baptism (QL3R-VJNJ), West Bromwich, 7 Oct 1879. Mother is Ann, NOT Hannah. Different Grice family. Thomas is not a child of Edwin Grice and Hannah Earnest. Ruled out.

Read Martha Emily Grice burial (QL7N-27ZN), Moxley, Staffordshire, 1887. Born 1885, died 1887. No parent names recorded in this burial register entry. Cannot confirm parentage. Moxley is adjacent to West Bromwich but a different parish; our family's known baptisms and deaths were registered in West Bromwich, making Moxley attribution uncertain. Will read the burial register image to check for parent names.

Attempted to read Moxley burial register image for Martha Emily Grice entry to check parent names. FamilySearch returned 403 Forbidden — image not accessible. Cannot confirm or rule out parentage of Martha Emily Grice (b.1885 Moxley, Staffordshire) through image inspection. The indexed record (QL7N-27ZN) carries no parent names; the image was the only remaining path.

Searched Staffordshire Church Records (2364451) for Hannah Grice baptism 1881–1884 with father Edwin. No record for a Hannah Grice child in this date range found among the 5 results. Results are unrelated records matching on Grice surname.
Broader Staffordshire Church Records search for Hannah Grice baptism 1881–1884, no father filter. Same 4 unrelated results; no Hannah Grice child baptism in this range found.
Searched GRO Birth Registration Index (2285338) for Hannah Grice born 1881–1884 in West Bromwich district. Zero results. No civil birth registration found for the second Hannah Grice.

Re-read second Hannah Grice death record (src_014) to check for parent names. Record confirms birth 1882, death 1883, West Bromwich. No parent names in GRO death index (standard limitation of this collection). Cannot confirm parentage from this record alone.

Broader GRO Birth Registration Index (2285338) search for Hannah Grice 1881–1884, no place restriction. Zero results across all of England. Birth registration for second Hannah Grice (d.1883 West Bromwich) is not indexed in FamilySearch's GRO birth index. Parentage established circumstantially: West Bromwich locality, date between first Hannah's 1881 death and Edwin's 1883 birth, Victorian re-naming practice.

quirks: Civil registration began 1 July 1837 at the England and Wales national level (Wolverhampton Registration District). Compliance was imperfect until 1874 when penalties were introduced — a birth c.1857 should be registered but may be missing; check adjacent quarters and adjacent districts (Penkridge, Walsall) if not found in Wolverhampton.

A christening date in a church register is the date of baptism, not the date of birth. Victorian Anglican practice often baptised children months or years after birth. The baptism register entry for 30 January 1868 must be viewed directly to read any stated birth date or age for the child.

The ancient parish of Wolverhampton St Peter (registers from 1603; Bishop's Transcripts from 1799) subdivided into at least ten daughter ecclesiastical parishes between 1832 and 1849. For events in 1850-1910, the correct parish register depends on which neighbourhood the family lived in — identify the address from a census return first.

Wolverhampton had active Nonconformist congregations (Wesleyan, Baptist, Independent, Presbyterian, Unitarian). Post-1837 Nonconformist baptism registers are not in the FamilySearch Staffordshire Church Records collection (CoE only); they are held by individual congregations or denominational archives.

Pre-1846 probate for Wolverhampton fell under the Court of the Peculiar of Wolverhampton; 1846-1858 under the Bishop of Lichfield's Consistory Court; from 1858 under the Principal Probate Registry (national). An index of wills at Wolverhampton Archives is downloadable at wolverhamptonhistory.org.uk.

The GRO's own free online birth index (gro.gov.uk) includes the mother's maiden name — a significant advantage over FreeBMD for distinguishing multiple children of the same name in the Wolverhampton district.
Surname spelling was unstandardised; search phonetic variants of Earnest (Ernest, Arnest) and Grice (Gryce) in all indexes.

The re-use of a given name within the same family almost always indicates the earlier child of that name died — a second 'Hannah' in a family register is evidence of infant death, not a duplicate record.
The 1891 census surname/folio index for the Wolverhampton district (including Bilston, Tettenhall, Wednesfield, Willenhall, Wombourn) compiled by BMSGH is at FamilySearch Library on film 6393534.
Civil registration events are filed by the date registered, not the date of the event. A birth in late December registered in January will appear in the following year's Q1 index.
